name: io.github.iowarp/graspa-mcp
title: CLIO Graspa
description: Gas adsorption in MOFs and zeolites by grand-canonical Monte Carlo with gRASPA: run, prepare for...

tools.name: run_graspa
tools.description: Compute the adsorption uptake of one gas (CO2, H2O or N2) in a framework CIF at a temperature (K) and pressure (Pa) by grand-canonical Monte Carlo with gRASPA, here. The cell is replicated so each width is at least twice the cutoff; the force field is UFF-like Lennard-Jones with TraPPE-style rigid adsorbates; framework charges 'none' (default) or 'cif'. Writes the run folder (inputs, gRASPA output, run.json, result.json) and reports the uptake in mol/kg with its block-average error bar and molecules per unit cell. Needs gRASPA and a GPU here (binary_missing otherwise; use prepare_graspa).

tools.name: prepare_graspa
tools.description: Write a gRASPA run folder (framework CIF, force field, adsorbate, simulation.input with the unit cells, run.json) for one adsorbate at a temperature and pressure, without running it: for a GPU node elsewhere (a Slurm job that runs gRASPA in the folder with stdout saved to graspa_stdout.txt). Same settings as run_graspa.

tools.name: read_graspa
tools.description: Read a finished gRASPA run folder (made by prepare_graspa or run_graspa, run here or on another machine): the uptake in mol/kg with its error bar, molecules per unit cell, mg/g, g/L and the Henry coefficient when gRASPA printed them. Writes result.json in the folder.

tools.name: rank_frameworks
tools.description: Rank frameworks from gRASPA results (result.json files or folders holding them; one adsorbate): by uptake at the adsorption condition, or, with a desorption condition, by working capacity (uptake at adsorption minus at desorption). Repeats are averaged; a framework without a completed run at every requested condition is excluded with the reason. Writes ranking.csv; top_fraction selects the best share.

tools.name: graspa_status
tools.description: Whether the gRASPA executable is available here, where it was found (GRASPA_COMMAND, CHEMGRAPH_GRASPA_EXECUTABLE or PATH), and how to get it.
